data.content:
The model also doesn’t know about injuries, suspensions, lineup news, weather, or motivational context. It’s a goals-based statistical estimate, not a football pundit. Always sanity-check before placing. If a top striker is unexpectedly out and the model still thinks the team will score goals, the bet flag may be invalid for reasons the math can’t see. [...] Use this page as a screening tool. Scan the day’s flagged bets, pick the matches you find interesting based on your own knowledge (lineups, recent form, weather, league context the model doesn’t see), and bet only those. This is the most labor-intensive approach but the most reliable for bettors who trust their own judgment alongside the math.

## Realistic Expectations for This Edge Range

Low-edge bets compound differently from high-edge bets. Here’s what to actually expect: [...] Both pages run on the same underlying Poisson model and pull from the same value bets database. The difference is in filter aggressiveness. Sweet Spot Method shows only edges between 16% and 35%, with additional filters on markets, day-of-week, and specific league exclusions — about 5-15 bets per day. Value Bets shows edges between 5% and 15% with simpler filtering — about 50-150 bets per day. Sweet Spot is curated for quality over quantity; Value Bets is the broader scanner output for bettors
